newsitem.title: INDIA: India cyclone devastates state paddy crop.
newsitem.headline: India cyclone devastates state paddy crop.

text.p: Up to 400,000 hectares (one million acres) of standing rice paddy crops have been hit by the devastating cyclone in the southeastern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, state agriculture ministry officials said on Friday.

"The affected area of paddy will be about 300,000 to 400,000 hectares in the east and west Godavari districts, the state's main rice bowl," Vasudev Reddy, additional director for natural calamities, told Reuters.
Speaking from the state capital Hyderabad, Reddy said: "Coconut and banana (crops) are more seriously affected. The extent of damage is not known. We are still awaiting information."
About 500,000 hectares (1.25 million acres) are under paddy cultivation in the two districts. In the whole state, nearly 2.6 million hectares (6.5 million acres) are under paddy.
Nageswara Rao, the Andhra Pradesh state government spokesman, told Reuters in that the Konaseema area of Hyderabad had been totally devastated.
He said the standing rice crop was awaiting harvesting when the cyclone hit on Wednesday night.
Most of the coconut crop has been wiped out, he added.
